inputs.question: Tell me about leave.
outputs.answer: Under UAE Labour Law, workers are entitled to annual leave with full pay. For full-time workers, this is 30 days per year of service, or 2 days per month for service between six months and one year [S1]. Part-time workers receive leave based on actual working hours, with a minimum of five working days per year, calculated proportionally [S3]. Leave must be taken in the year it is earned, but may be carried forward to the next year if approved by the employer, up to half the annual leave [S4]. Employers must notify workers of leave dates at least one month in advance [S1]. If a worker leaves before using leave, they are entitled to wages for unused leave days [S2].

inputs.question: My employer has not paid my salary for two months. What does the law say?
outputs.answer: If your employer has not paid your salary for two months, the law requires that wages be paid on due dates through the Wage Protection System or an approved system [S1]. The Ministry may take legal action against the employer for non-payment of agreed wages [S1]. You have the right to file a complaint with the Ministry, which can enforce payment and impose penalties on the employer [S1].

inputs.question: What did the 2022 amendment change in the Labour Law?
outputs.answer: The 2022 Amendment changed clause (3) of Article (8) of the UAE Labour Law, replacing it to state that the employment contract shall be concluded for a definite period, renewable, based upon the parties' agreement [S1]. This amendment clarifies that fixed-term contracts are the standard and can be renewed by mutual agreement [S1]. The amendment was published in the Official Gazette and came into force the day after its publication [S3]. Any conflicting provisions in previous laws were repealed [S2].

inputs.question: Can my company send my personal data to another country?
outputs.answer:
Your company can send your personal data to another country only if one of the following conditions is met under the UAE Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL):

- The receiving country has adequate data protection laws, and the transfer is approved by the UAE Data Protection Bureau [S2].
- There is explicit consent from you (the data subject) to transfer your data, provided it does not harm public or national security [S1][S2].
- The transfer is necessary to fulfill a contract between your employer and you, or to protect public interest, legal rights, or for international judicial cooperation [S1].

If none of these conditions apply, the transfer is not permitted [S1][S2].
outputs.sources: ['UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021), Article 23', 'UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021), Article 22']

inputs.question: Do I have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit?
outputs.answer: No, you do not have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit in the UAE. Labour lawsuits are exempt from judicial fees at all stages of litigation and execution, including requests valued at or below 100,000 AED [S1].

inputs.question: What does Article 51 say?
outputs.answer: Article 51 of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) outlines the end-of-service gratuity for full-time workers. It states that foreign full-time workers who have completed one or more years of continuous service are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity calculated based on their basic wage: 21 days' wage for each year of the first five years, and 30 days' wage for each year beyond that [S3]. The gratuity is calculated using the last basic wage received, or the average daily wage for piece-rate workers, and must not exceed two years' wage [S3][S4]. Days of absence without pay are not included in the service calculation [S3]. Employers may deduct lawful or court-ordered amounts from the gratuity, as per the Executive Regulation [S4]. The Cabinet may approve alternative gratuity systems with specific conditions [S4].

inputs.question: How much notice must be given to end an employment contract?
outputs.answer: The notice period, known as the warning period, must be between thirty (30) days and ninety (90) days, as specified in the employment contract [S1]. This period must be observed by either party when terminating the contract for a legitimate reason [S1]. The warning period remains effective until its expiry, during which the worker must continue working if requested by the employer [S1]. If the warning period is not followed, the non-complying party must pay a warning allowance equal to the worker’s wage for the full or remaining warning period [S1].

inputs.question: What is the maximum probation period?
outputs.answer: The maximum probation period is six (6) months [S1].
outputs.sources: ['UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), Article 9']
outputs.rewritten: What is the maximum duration of the probationary period?
outputs.context:
["[Labour Law — Article 9, part 1/2]
Article (9)
Probation Period
1. The Employer may appoint the Worker under the Probation Period for a period not
exceeding six (6) months as of the date of commencing work, and he may terminate the
Worker's service during this period after notifying the Worker in writing at least fourteen
(14) days prior to the date specified for termination of service.
2. A Worker may not be appointed under probation more than once with one employer, and
if the Worker successfully passes the Probation Period and continues to work, the contract
becomes valid in accordance with the terms agreed upon, and that period must be
counted within the service period.
3. In the event that the Worker wishes to move, during the Probation Period, to work for
another employer in the State, he must notify the original Employer in writing within a
period not less than one month as of the date of his desire to terminate the contract. The
new Employer shall compensate the original Employer with the costs of recruiting or
contracting with the Worker, unless agreed otherwise.
4. In the event that the foreign Worker wishes to terminate the employment contract, during
the Probation Period, to leave the State, he must notify the Employer in writing, at least
(14) fourteen days prior to the date specified for the termination of the co ntract. And in
the event that he wishes to return to the State and obtain a new work permit within three
(3) months as of the date of leaving, the new Employer shall pay the compensation", "[Labour Law — Article 29, part 1/2]

Annual leave

enforcement of the provisions of this Decree by law, the Worker shall be entitled to an
annual leave with full pay of not less than:
a. Thirty days for each year of his extended service.
b. Two days for each month if his service period is more than six months and less than
one year.

before using his annual leave balance.

inputs.question: How many sick leave days am I entitled to, and are they paid?
outputs.answer:
After the probation period, you are entitled to a maximum of 90 sick leave days per year, calculated as follows:  
- First 15 days: full pay [S1].  
- Next 30 days: half pay [S1].  
- Remaining 45 days: unpaid [S1].  
Sick leave is not paid if the illness results from the worker’s misconduct, as specified in the Executive Regulation [S1].

outputs.context:
["[Labour Law — Article 31]

a. The first fifteen (15) days with full pay.
b. The following thirty (30) days with half pay.
c. The following period shall be unpaid.

accordance with the cases specified in the Executive Regulation of this Decree by law.

intermittently, within a period of six (6) months as of the date of the child's birth.
c. Any other leaves determined by the Cabinet.
2. The Worker may be granted a study leave for a period of ten (10) business days per year,
for the Worker who is enrolled - by affiliation or regularly - in one of the educational
institutions approved in the State, in order to perform the tests, provided th at the period
of service with the Employer is not less than two years.

Maternity Leave

due to an illness suffered by her or her child as a result of pregnancy or childbirth and that
does not enable her to return to her work. Said illness shall be proven by a medical
certificate issued by the Medical Authority, and this period shall not be included in the
period of service for which the female Worker is entitled to the end of service gratui ty or
